title: El fin de semana pasado
blurbEn: A trip to the mountains, told with -er and -ir verbs — which share one set of endings between them.
body:
El fin de semana pasado salí de la ciudad con dos amigos.

El sábado cogimos el tren muy temprano y viajamos hasta un pueblo pequeño en la montaña.

Comimos en un restaurante muy barato y bebimos un vino muy bueno. Después subimos hasta un lago y nadamos un poco.

El domingo volvimos a casa muy tarde. Escribí un mensaje a mi hermana y le mandé unas fotos.

Quiero volver pronto.
translationEn:
Last weekend I left the city with two friends.

On Saturday we caught the train very early and travelled to a small village in the mountains.

We ate in a very cheap restaurant and drank a very good wine. Afterwards we walked up to a lake and swam a little.

On Sunday we came home very late. I wrote a message to my sister and sent her some photos.

I want to go back soon.

cogimos.note: Everyday in Spain for taking transport. In much of Latin America 'tomar' is used instead, and 'coger' is best avoided.

comimos.note: Identical to the present 'we eat'. Only the sentence tells you which — here, 'el sábado'.

phrases.note: 'pasado' after the noun means 'last'. It is one of the clearest signals for this tense.
